bib.title: Personalizing Dialogue Agents: I have a dog, do you have pets too?
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 56th Annual Meeting of the ACL (Long Papers), pages 2204-2213

read.skipped: Nothing skipped, but this 10-page camera-ready PDF does not contain the appendices (Tables 5-14, Appendix D, human-eval question wording) that the text refers to.

question: Can conditioning chit-chat agents on explicit textual profile information (their own and their partner's) make dialogue more consistent and engaging, and can a crowd-sourced persona-conditioned dataset support this?
hypothesis: Conditioning on persona information gives improved prediction of the next dialogue utterance and more consistent, engaging responses than persona-free models.
contributions: The PERSONA-CHAT crowd-sourced dataset of persona-conditioned dialogues with original and revised (word-distinct) personas
Baseline ranking and generative models, including profile memory networks, evaluated on next-utterance prediction with and without personas
Human evaluation comparing PERSONA-CHAT models with Twitter and OpenSubtitles trained models, and preliminary profile prediction

method.summary: Crowdworkers on Amazon Mechanical Turk wrote personas, rewrote them without word overlap, and then chatted in pairs while playing assigned personas. Ranking (IR, Starspace, profile memory, KV profile memory) and generative (Seq2Seq, generative profile memory) models are scored on next-utterance prediction under no/own/their/both persona conditions, plus a Turker human evaluation.
method.task: next-utterance prediction in persona-conditioned chit-chat dialogue

datasets.name: PERSONA-CHAT
datasets.size: 164,356 utterances over 10,981 dialogs; 1155 personas of at least 5 profile sentences
datasets.split: validation 15,705 utterances (968 dialogs); test 15,119 utterances (1000 dialogs); 100 never-seen personas each for validation and test
datasets.source: Amazon Mechanical Turk; open source in ParlAI (licence not stated in the text)
datasets.preprocessing: Persona sentences max 15 words; messages max 15 words; minimum dialogue length random between 6 and 8 turns each; string-matching error if persona text copied; revised personas warn on copied non-stop words

datasets.name: Twitter
datasets.source: used to train comparison LM chit-chat models (Vinyals and Le 2015 style)

datasets.name: OpenSubtitles (2009 and 2018 versions)
datasets.source: used to train comparison LM and KV Memory models

models.name: IR baseline
models.architecture: tf-idf weighted cosine similarity between bags of words; returns the response of the most similar training message

other.persona: concatenated to the query bag of words

models.name: Starspace
models.architecture: sum of word embeddings, cosine similarity, margin ranking loss with k-negative sampling

other.persona: concatenated to the query bag of words

models.name: Ranking Profile Memory Network
models.architecture: Starspace representation and loss; one hop of softmax attention over profile sentences: q+ = q + sum s_i p_i

other.hops: multiple hops gave no significant gains in parameter sweeps

models.name: KV Profile Memory Network
models.architecture: profile memory first hop, second hop attends over keys (training dialogue histories) and outputs weighted sum of values (next utterances)
models.init_from: weights of the trained Profile Memory network, applied only at test time

models.name: Seq2Seq
models.architecture: LSTM encoder-decoder, persona prepended to input

other.note: for Twitter and OpenSubtitles a language model (decoder only) worked better and is reported

models.name: Generative Profile Memory Network
models.architecture: LSTM encoder-decoder; decoder attends over encoded profile entries, each encoded as inverse-term-frequency weighted word sum

training.objective: Seq2Seq and generative models: negative log likelihood; ranking models: margin ranking loss with k-negative sampling (Starspace loss)

other.training_persona_variants: trained with original or revised personas; comparison in appendix Table 6, not in this PDF

inference.retrieval: ranking models rank candidate utterances (any training-set utterance for ranking; 19 random distractors plus the correct one for hits@1)

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.definition: log likelihood of the correct sequence

metrics.name: hits@1
metrics.definition: correct reply among N=19 random distractors from other dialogues; 1 if model picks the correct one, else 0

metrics.name: fluency, engagingness, consistency
metrics.definition: Turker ratings after chatting with the model

metrics.name: persona detection
metrics.definition: Turker picks which of two profiles is more likely the model's

eval.protocol: Automatic: four persona conditions (none, own, their, both) x original/revised personas. Human: Turkers paired with a model without knowing, 100 dialogues each; std reported, no significance test, rater counts and agreement not stated.

availability.weights: models trained on the data available in ParlAI

limits: Appendix tables (their persona, both personas, original vs revised training, example chats) and human-eval question wording are not in this PDF.
Authors concede human-eval differences are 'obscured by the high variance of the human raters' evaluations'; no significance tests or rater counts.
Models trained in a heuristic way (KV memory uses weights from Profile Memory network); training hyperparameters are not given.
Authors note results depend on crowdworker instructions: 'Using Their persona has less impact' because speakers focus on themselves.
Full profile prediction study is stated to be beyond the scope.
